## 1. Packages

```{r}
#| label: packages
# pacman::p_load() installs a package if it is missing, then loads it
pacman::p_load(tidyverse, here, janitor)
```

## 2. Question and data

**Question:** [One question that names a group, a measure and a period.]

**Expected message:** [One sentence.]

**Source:** see `data/raw/SOURCE.md`.

```{r}
#| label: data
#| eval: false
# Load the original file once into a named object, then start every later chunk from it.
# here() builds the path from the project folder, so it works on any computer.
# read_csv() reads a csv file. clean_names() makes column names lowercase with underscores.
my_data <- here("data", "raw", "my_data.csv") |>
  read_csv(show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  clean_names()

# head() prints the first 6 rows
my_data |>
  head()
```

## 3. Exploration

Write one line under each result that says what you learned.

```{r}
#| label: explore-structure
#| eval: false
# glimpse() lists each column with its type, so you see numbers, text and dates at once
my_data |>
  glimpse()
```

```{r}
#| label: explore-missing
#| eval: false
# summarise(across(...)) counts the missing values in every column
my_data |>
  summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sum(is.na(x)))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column", values_to = "n_missing")
```

```{r}
#| label: explore-distribution
#| eval: false
# One variable: histogram (replace x with your variable)
my_data |>
  ggplot(aes(x = variable)) +
  geom_histogram()
```

## 4. Wrangling

Use at least 5 different verbs (for example `filter()`, `mutate()`, `case_when()`, `group_by()`, `summarise()`, `pivot_longer()`, `left_join()`). Add a comment above each one that says why you use it.

```{r}
#| label: wrangle
#| eval: false
my_data |>
  filter() |>      # keep only the rows needed for the question
  mutate() |>      # create or change a column
  group_by() |>    # run the next step once per group
  summarise()      # one row per group
```

## 6. Final graph

Refine one graph: title that states the finding, axis labels with units, ordered categories, one highlight color, no clutter.

```{r}
#| label: final-graph
#| eval: false
my_data |>
  ggplot(aes()) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(
    title = "[the finding as a sentence]",
    x = NULL,
    y = "[measure and unit]",
    caption = "Source: [data source]"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# ggsave() saves the last graph as an image for story.md
ggsave(here("figures", "final_graph.png"), width = 8, height = 4.5, dpi = 300)
```
